independence.reviewBasis: Actual source pixels, full frozen edition prose and captions, both current FigureSpecs, and all six existing exact-SVG Chromium screenshots together.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: One upright fork with two long nearly level-ended arms, a long open slot, and a rounded common lower neck. Neither arm is broken or detached.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: The browser images preserve both separate arms and the open slot joining into one lower neck at every inspected width. Exact parallelism and equal lengths are a disclosed schematic regularization, not measurements from the scan.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: The common neck narrows into a short vertical stem, ending on a small oval mounting foot on the box top. It is one mounted apparatus, not a hovering fork.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: At 640, 331 and 342 px the neck, stem and oval foot visibly touch; the foot sits on the narrow support spanning the opening. The current coordinates also place the fork bottom at screen y=283, stem at y=281..305, and foot around y=305, corroborating contact rather than substituting objectCount for the visual inspection.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: One perspective rectangular box with a broad top, long front face, small left end face, joined edges and source face hatching. The source top looks mostly blank around the mount, rather than depicting a clearly bounded cavity.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: The same three-face structure and continuous edges remain. Neutral face shading replaces print hatching. The dark inset is an opening surrounded by a white rim, not a black-filled entire box. The wooden material label is readable.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: A printing rectangle encloses the scan. No visible text, numeric measurement, hammer, needle, plate, second fork, arrow, wave ray or axis is drawn.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: The printing border is omitted; only the disclosed English identifiers are added. No recording apparatus, hammer, second resonance experiment, motion direction or answer-bearing annotation is invented.

editionAndPhysicalFidelity.apparatus: Frozen EN prose[2] and caption[4] explicitly say a fork fixed to a wooden box open at the top; ZH states the same. The scan does not clearly show that opening. The edition is authoritative: the inset opening and narrow bridge reconcile that text with the source-mounted foot while preserving a single apparatus.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.mountingBridge: The bridge is explicitly a modern construction clarification, not a source fact or a measured acoustic mechanism. It visibly connects to the rim at both ends and supports the foot, so the fork is not shown suspended over an unsupported hole.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.recordingProcedure: The surrounding text describes a needle on one arm and uniform sliding over soot-blackened glass; neither the source FIG81 nor this modern FIG81 claims to show that procedure. Its omission is not missing source apparatus.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.measurements: No source dimensions, frequency, amplitude scale or numeric data exist in this figure. None is invented. Parallelism and matched tine length are appropriate identified schematic regularizations, not new measured givens.

browserVisualReview.result: All parts remain legible and joined. No clipping, label collision, missing outline, unwanted fill, cultural lettering or answer disclosure is visible.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: One connected, solid, thick oscillatory line in the middle band of one horizontal rectangular frame. Six upper crests and seven lower troughs are visible, giving six complete trough-to-trough cycles.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: All three Chromium widths show the same single solid line with six crests and seven troughs, no extra trace, dash, interruption, intersection or added cycle. Counts were checked in the source and browser pixels, not inferred from the single-path assertion.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: The left endpoint starts around the middle height and descends to the first trough. After the seventh trough the right endpoint rises toward the middle height and stops before a seventh crest. Both endpoints lie inside the frame.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: The modern left partial segment descends and the right partial segment rises, with neither extended to a further crest. Both have visible clearance from the enclosing frame at desktop and mobile widths.

sourcePixelInventory.observed: One shared rectangular enclosure, with no axes, baseline, ticks, numbers, units, arrows, labels, needle, plate-motion drawing or separate subfigure.
sourcePixelInventory.comparison: The shared enclosure remains, with only the disclosed English Time trace identifier added above the curve. The label does not cross the frame or curve. No axis, calibration or invented apparatus appears.

editionAndPhysicalFidelity.meaning: Frozen prose[2] and caption[6] identify a nearly sinusoidal time trace of the fork's vibration obtained by uniform sliding. The curve is used as that time record, not as an additional acoustic propagation diagram.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.regularization: The deterministic trace regularizes small printed spacing/amplitude irregularities into a smooth repeated curve. This is disclosed as schematic, with no measured amplitude or period claimed. It preserves the source's qualitative near-sinusoidal shape, visible extrema counts and endpoint directions.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.damping: Although the preceding prose says vibration gradually decays, the actual source FIG82 itself shows roughly constant-height cycles in this short trace. Retaining that source schematic does not assert a quantitative undamped motion or replace it with an invented decay envelope.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.frequencyAndScale: Six cycles do not establish a numerical frequency without a time calibration. No calibration, frequency, amplitude, sign, unit or answer is added. The label and surrounding prose identify the time interpretation.
editionAndPhysicalFidelity.assertionLimit: The spec's objectCount and rectangular-frame assertions cannot prove oscillation count or endpoint fidelity. This independent source/browser comparison and the separately derived current M/L path extrema provide those missing semantic observations.

browserVisualReview.result: Six crests, seven troughs and the partial endpoints remain visible and separated from the frame. The curve is not missing, black-filled or clipped, and the label remains readable.

rasterDiagnostic.verdict: Unusable generic width-preview mechanism for these exact semantic-variable SVG bytes, not an actual FIG81/82 geometry, stroke or fill defect in the inspected Chromium rendering.
rasterDiagnostic.cause: The bound generic tool reads the raw SVG and passes it directly to new Resvg(svg, opts), with white background and fitTo width but no CSS-variable resolution. These SVGs intentionally use var(--ld-figure-*, fallback) semantic colors. The retained author failure records report dropped var()-stroked paths and paper regions filled black. The exact unchanged SVG bytes produce the intended dark strokes and white paper in the existing Chromium captures with resolved computed styles. This local contrast identifies the CSS-variable paint-handling mismatch in the generic Resvg preview path; it is not a claim about every resvg version or every SVG.
rasterDiagnostic.initialSpecFailure: FIG81's original collinear assertion encoded points rather than a/b/c. Its retained initial draft FAIL consumed the sole repair; current geometry is unchanged. This encoding failure is distinct from the later generic width-preview paint failure.
rasterDiagnostic.disposition: Keep the original author FAIL/HOLD, its exact failed PNGs/receipts, and initial assertion failure unchanged. Add independent PASS for the current source/spec/render/output binding based on actual Chromium pixels; do not silently reinterpret failed PNGs as usable.

gateLimits.otherDeclaredWidths: 346, 480 and 358 px retain their existing passing native displayChecks; no fresh visual capture is claimed for those widths.
gateLimits.recordReviewOnly: If recorded, each review@1 gate binds the current native render report and unchanged SVG. Its standard in-process integrity validation is part of recording, not a native renderer or separate validation command rerun.
gateLimits.textAuthority: D050 repair-freeze plus affected-review are authoritative. The usual-amplitude qualifier is the only repaired prose sentence; SCI and effective ZHEN remain inherited PASS, not repeated here. The retained numeric-declaration blocker is not cleared by this figure review.
